Goals.Goal: **The `--explain` fallback is honest about what it searched (`F255`, code half, in `src/grace-lint.ts`).** On the undotted path, when the token is not a registered shape and is not the last segment of any registered code, the text first line is `Unknown code or shape: <token>` and the `Registered shapes:` sentence that follows is byte-unchanged. When it is the last segment of two or more, the first line names each candidate: `Unknown code or shape: <token>; candidates: <a>, <b>, …` — it never guesses one. Exit stays 1. The JSON form becomes `{ "kind": "unknown-code-or-shape", "token": <token>, "suggestedCodes": [ … ], "registered": [ … ] }` — `kind` no longer asserts the token was treated as a shape, and the candidate list is machine-readable. The dotted unknown path (`not.a.real.code` → Lint Issue Guide, `Classification: unknown`, exit 1) and the shape path are unchanged. The registered-code universe is the concrete codes `--explain` can answer from — the exact-guide keys plus the review and gate catalogs — and the suggestion is the subset of those whose last dot-segment equals the token, in sorted order.

**One id per claim, everywhere the anchor key is per-target (`F256`).** Every `makeFinding` site in `src/review/core.ts` whose `anchorOrHunkKey` is derived from a value that can repeat within one artifact rather than from the claim's position is repaired so that two claims never share an id: `must-exist:${target}` (`:548`), `marker:${marker}` (`:496`), `must-match:${file}` (`:623`) and `vm-child:${node.tag}:${child.tag}` (`:889`). The chosen remedy is **position in the key**: the key carries a document-order discriminator unique among that rule's emits in the file, so each claim keeps its own finding and its own id. The review's reported finding count equals its distinct-id count for every `review.*` code, and `--ack-finding` for outcome `pass` remains one-for-one with the displayed findings, so acknowledging one claim can never silently cover a different one. The de-duplication-with-a-count remedy is rejected: it recreates the same one-ack-covers-two-claims defect at the message level, and it lets a claim be acknowledged that the reviewer has not fixed.

**The green run names the commands it ran (`F257`, in `src/lint/core.ts`).** When a lint run evaluates commands, `formatTextReport` emits one line `Commands: <N> evaluated, <M> exit 0`, where `N` is the number of commands the run spawned and `M` is the number that exited 0; all-pass reads `Commands: <N> evaluated, <N> exit 0`. The line is sourced from module-private state keyed on the result per `D13`; `LintResult` gains no field, `M-LINT-TYPES` stays out of `AffectedAreas`, and `--format json` gains no top-level key. The line appends without altering any byte `C-LINT-PHASE-HONESTY-2` pins: the `Errors:`/`Warnings:` lines, the singular and plural structural-query note, and the current-mode baseline lead stay byte-identical, and the line appears only when commands were actually evaluated.
